records.author: Hector_Lenovo
records.text:
Hi HuniKha!
Thank you for reaching out to the Lenovo Community. Sorry to hear about your experience and I understand the concern with your external monitor brightness dimming after some time, especially since it returns when you power the monitor off/on or toggle HDR.
Since the brightness returns when you power the monitor off and on, or when you toggle HDR, the best path is to check the display and graphics settings in order.
1. First, turn off any automatic brightness controls on your laptop:
- Open Settings > System > Display.
- Look for Brightness settings and turn off Adaptive brightness, Change brightness automatically, or similar power-saving dimming options if present.
- If your system has HDR enabled, turn HDR off temporarily and test the monitor for more than 40 minutes.
2. Check the external monitor’s own on-screen menu:
- Disable any setting such as Dynamic Contrast / DCR, Auto HDR, Eco Mode.
- If the monitor has a local dimming or automatic power-saving feature, turn that off as well.
3. Reseat the video connection:
- Disconnect and reconnect the cable on both ends.
- If possible, test with a different cable.
- If available, try another port type such as HDMI instead of USB-C/DisplayPort, or vice versa.
4. Check refresh rate and HDR format:
- Go to Settings > System > Display > Advanced display.
- Select the external monitor and test a standard refresh rate such as 60 Hz.
- If HDR is enabled, test with HDR off first. If the issue stops, it is likely related to the HDR handshake or display processing.
5. Isolate whether the issue is with the monitor or the laptop:
- Test the same monitor with another computer for at least 40 minutes.
- If the dimming still happens, the monitor is likely causing it.
- If it only happens with your laptop, the issue is more likely related to the laptop’s graphics settings, driver, or signal output.
If you’ve already tried different cables and HDR settings, let us know your monitor connection type (HDMI, USB-C, or DisplayPort) and whether the dimming happens only on the external monitor or also on your laptop screen if you're using one.
We will be waiting for your response.
Best regards,
Hector_Lenovo

records.source_title: HDR Dimming Issue on Lenovo Legion Pro, Can't Update Firmware 27Q-10
records.author: Hector_Lenovo
records.text:
Thanks for the update!
1. On the monitor OSD, switch from HDR Auto/Movie/Photo (Peak 1000) to another HDR mode if available, especially True Black 400, then test for at least 40 to 60 minutes. If the dimming only happens in Peak 1000 modes, that helps isolate the issue to that HDR mode behavior.
2. In Windows, turn HDR off, restart the PC, then turn HDR back on and set the monitor as the only active display during testing. If you use multiple monitors, disconnect the others temporarily to rule out HDR mode negotiation issues.
3. Set the refresh rate to a standard test value such as 144 Hz or 120 Hz at the monitor’s native resolution, then retest HDR. This helps check whether the issue is tied to the current high-bandwidth display setting.
4. If you are using any graphics software features such as Auto HDR, RTX HDR, AMD video enhancements, dynamic contrast, content-adaptive brightness, or color enhancement, disable them and test again. Also leave Windows HDR/SDR balance at the default position during testing.
5. Reset the monitor OSD settings to factory defaults, then enable HDR again and test only one HDR picture mode at a time. Do not enable additional image enhancements while testing.
6. Install Lenovo Artery if you have not already, and check whether the monitor is detected there. If available, confirm the current monitor software or driver package shown by the app and apply any offered monitor-related update from within the app rather than through manual Have Disk installation. You can download the tool
here
.
7. About the file you downloaded: the .inf package is a monitor driver/extension package, not the same as a direct firmware flash utility. If Windows reports that the folder does not contain a compatible driver, perhaps you can try extracting both x64 and x86 folder file to Desktop then try again.
Best regards,
Hector_Lenovo

records.text:
Hello EnDelt,
Welcome to Lenovo Community
I understand that the built-in speakers of your
Yoga Pro 27UD-10
monitor are having issues wherein it stops working or behave unpredictably after wake or over USB4.
Based on what you described, this may involve the monitor’s audio path resetting incorrectly after sleep/wake or when the USB4 connection reinitializes. Since the speakers recover after power-cycling the monitor, that suggests the monitor, connection handshake, or audio routing may need further investigation rather than this pointing only to a Windows volume setting.
Here are some steps you can try now:
1. In Windows 11, after the issue happens, go to Sound Settings and confirm the monitor is still selected as the active output device.
2. In Device Manager, remove the audio output entry associated with the monitor, then restart the computer so Windows reloads it.
3. Test with a different cable (Lenovo cables are highly recommended) if available, even if the current one appears to work for display and charging.
4. If the monitor has multiple input methods available, test another connection type temporarily to see whether the issue is limited to one path.
5. On the MacBook Pro, after the loudness jump or audio loss occurs, recheck Sound Output and test whether disconnecting and reconnecting only the USB4 cable changes the behavior before power-cycling the monitor.
6. If available in your setup, test the monitor with one device at a time to rule out switching-related behavior.
7. Check the monitor’s on-screen menu for any audio-related settings and make sure volume, mute, and input-related audio options remain stable after wake.
8. Ensure that your monitor's firmware and driver are up to date. See the
support page
for latest available updates.
Test, observe and let me know how things go. Besides the MacBook Pro, please indicate what computer are you using. If possible, kindly include the full MTM (machine type model), BIOS and OS build version.
Best regards,
Lorenzo_Lenovo

In Windows 11, if I enable the “Turn off my screen after” setting, there are times when the audio stops working after the display turns off and then wakes up again. The volume level and Windows sound settings still appear to be normal.
